sahneler.metin: This mountain lost 1,300 feet of its top in minutes.
Its north side collapsed in the largest landslide ever recorded.
But for weeks, Mount Saint Helens had bulged five feet a day.
Scientists measured it, but nobody knew exactly when it would fail.
When it slid away, the trapped pressure blasted out sideways.
The blast flattened 230 square miles of forest.
Mudflows then wiped out 27 bridges downstream.
Fifty-seven people died. It rewrote how volcanoes are watched.

aciklama:
On May 18, 1980, the bulging north flank of Mount St. Helens collapsed in the largest landslide ever recorded, releasing a sideways blast.
